title: Coset Lifted Product Codes: Constructing Quantum LDPC Codes from Non-Normal Subgroup Actions
authors: Rajendra Prasad Rajpurohit, V. Lalitha, Shayan Srinivasa Garani
abstract: We introduce coset lifted product (CLP) codes, a family of quantum LDPC codes that combine the protograph structure of lifted product codes with the coset action of Aydin, Tamo, and Barg \cite{AydinTamoBarg2026}. Given a finite group $G$, a subgroup $H \le G$ that need not be normal, a protograph $A$ over $\mathbb F_2[G]$, and a protograph $B$ over $\mathbb F_2[N_G(H)]$, the two protographs act on the cosets $G/H$ from the left and from the right to produce quantum CSS codes. Further, for groups of odd order, we give an explicit formula for the dimension as a sum over the irreducible representations $ρ$ of $G$ of hypergraph product dimensions. A search over $14,843$ pairs $(G,H)$ with $H$ restricted to be non-normal and $120 \le n \le 400$ yields certified codes that exceed the best published value of $Q=kd^2/n$ at check weights $6,7$ and $9$, i.e., we obtain $[[360,20,20]]$ at $w=6$, a $[[360,24,20]]$ code at $w=7$, and codes $[[252,16,18]]$ and $[[288,16,20]]$ at $w=9$. Our search also produce high-distance codes with parameters $[[168,10,14]], [[240,8,20]]$ at $w=6$ and $[[216,8,18]]$ at $w=7$.
summary: This paper introduces Coset Lifted Product (CLP) codes, a new family of quantum LDPC codes built using group theory and coset actions. By systematically searching over various group structures, the authors construct and certify quantum codes with parameters that surpass current state-of-the-art bounds. This provides a powerful, general algebraic method for designing high-performance quantum error correction codes.
main_problem: The paper focuses on constructing quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes using a novel algebraic framework.
main_result: They introduce Coset Lifted Product (CLP) codes, demonstrating that a systematic search over group pairs yields certified quantum codes exceeding previously known bounds on the quality metric Q.
method: The construction combines protograph structures with the coset action of a subgroup $H$ within a finite group $G$, leading to the definition of the parity-check matrices $H_X$ and $H_Z$.
model_or_system: The model is the quantum error-correcting code, specifically a CSS code, defined by two classical linear codes whose parity-check matrices satisfy the orthogonality condition $H_X H_Z^T = 0$.
key_observables: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$, the code rate $k/n$, and the quality metric $Q = kd^2/n$.
important_parameters: The construction depends on a finite group $G$, a subgroup $H \le G$ (which need not be normal), and associated protographs $A$ and $B$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of the group algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[G]$ and relies on algebraic techniques involving coset actions and representation theory for dimension calculation.
figures_summary: No specific figures are described, but the notes detail the algebraic structure of the parity-check matrices derived from group actions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically defines the CLP code construction, proves it satisfies the CSS condition, derives dimension formulas for odd order groups, and culminates in a large-scale search yielding concrete, high-performing code examples.
why_interesting: The work provides a powerful, general algebraic tool for constructing quantum codes, moving beyond standard constructions by incorporating non-normal subgroup actions, which is highly relevant for designing robust quantum memory and communication protocols.
